S1.title: NASA Science: Lake Nyos, Cameroon
S1.supports: Date, northwestern Cameroon, crater, geological CO2 supply, broad event framing.

S2.title: Kling et al. (1987), Science: The 1986 Lake Nyos Gas Disaster
S2.supports: At least 1700 deaths, CO2 asphyxiation, dissolved reservoir, magmatic origin, no significant direct volcanic activity.

S3.title: Kling, Evans & Tanyileke (2015): Comparative limnology
S3.supports: Weak deep mixing, persistent lower-water isolation, gradual dissolved CO2 buildup; rarity.

S4.title: Zhang (1996): Dynamics of CO2-driven lake eruptions
S4.supports: Physical explanation of CO2-driven release; pressure/bubble mechanism. Bottle is an explanatory analogy, not an assertion of identical systems.

S5.title: Chan, Kwok & Mak (1996): A model of gas buildup and release in crater lakes
S5.supports: Dissolved gas, release dynamics, triggering hypotheses; model-specific predictions not adopted.

S6.title: IPCC Special Report on Carbon Dioxide Capture and Storage, chapter 6, box 6.7
S6.supports: Lake Nyos CO2 hazard and its behaviour after release; general concentration/terrain explanation.

S7.title: NASA SVS: Lake Nyos Zoom-in (2002)
S7.supports: Reported deadly effects as far as 25 km; Landsat imagery dated 2001-02-05.

S8.title: Kling et al. (1987), full paper; and Cotel (1999), A trigger mechanism
S8.supports: Trigger unknown in investigation; later proposed mechanisms remain hypotheses, not a witnessed reconstruction.

S9.title: Kling et al. (2005): Degassing Lakes Nyos and Monoun
S9.supports: Nyos degassing started in 2001; gas removal, pipe operation and changing rates.

S10.title: USGS 2005 degassing findings and 2015 comparative limnology
S10.supports: Measured gas reduction, no dangerous water-column destabilization observed; continued gas recharge and monitoring.
